checks.workload: Seven temporal equality histories, two completion choices, three persistent providers.
checks.invariant: PostgreSQL equality, conflict outcomes and committed values; each history remains independently bounded by the CI stall limit.

checks.workload: Four providers; 16/64 unrelated parents, 100/20000-byte child bodies, CASCADE/NO ACTION, zero/two matches.
checks.invariant: Zero child enumerations and exactly the matched number of child document reads; SQL effects and errors remain correct.

checks.workload: Indexed referential-action PostgreSQL reference cases on four providers.
checks.invariant: Values, errors, rollback and reopen match the independent PostgreSQL reference.

checks.workload: Four providers; repeated parameterized INSERT, rollback, duplicate-key failure and column rename.
checks.invariant: Data changes retain the identical parsed statement; returned rows, rollback, unique violations and fresh schema errors match PostgreSQL.

checks.workload: 32 generic calls, DISCARD, 32 auto calls, four custom calls and routine replacement.
checks.invariant: Generic preparation folds once, auto adds six evaluations and four custom calls add four; DISCARD and replacement refresh output correctly.

checks.workload: 32 loop iterations plus static cursor and dynamic EXECUTE cases.
checks.invariant: Static generic plans fold once, two cursor sources twice, dynamic EXECUTE 32 times, with output checks.

checks.workload: 10000 rows, k=7 and a 4096-byte allowance with an unusable spill directory.
checks.invariant: Exact stable top-seven output, one initial run and zero merge passes.

checks.workload: 73 rows, four budgets, four result limits, both orderings and NULL placements.
checks.invariant: Bounded results equal full-sort results in every combination.

checks.workload: A 260-document occurrence cluster, one selected document and unrelated retained memory.
checks.invariant: Peak equals selected output bytes plus seven retained bytes; missing rows and corruption are still checked.

checks.workload: Every byte allowance up to successful phrase production with earlier live results.
checks.invariant: Quota failures release only failed work; prior results, occurrence semantics and budget ownership survive.

checks.workload: Score-cursor WAND and block-max WAND versus materialized WAND.
checks.invariant: Selected identities and scores match the complete reference path.

checks.workload: 20 vectors of 1024 dimensions with a 64-KiB allowance.
checks.invariant: Spill preserves resident topology, scores, mutation and retained-reader results under the original allowance.

checks.workload: 400 vectors of 128 dimensions with a 128-KiB allowance and mutation replay.
checks.invariant: Centroids and assignments match resident execution; peak never exceeds the original allowance.

checks.workload: Graph-page fragments served through counted provider batches.
checks.invariant: Reported requests and actual provider batches agree with the deterministic fixture.

checks.workload: Generation construction at memory and artifact allowance boundaries.
checks.invariant: Admission failures retain neither partial output nor leaked capture reservations.

checks.workload: 1-MiB unrelated properties and keys under a 16-KiB retained allowance.
checks.invariant: Indexed identity/count results remain correct without hydrating unrelated properties; requested corrupt payloads still fail.

checks.workload: 31 reserve warm-up allocations followed by 32 managed allocations.
checks.invariant: Exactly two synchronized allocation commits for the final 32 IDs; every receipt is independently visible and IDs are never reused.

checks.workload: 32 and 128 validated new records with SQLite VM-step counting.
checks.invariant: Seeding absent originals executes zero SQLite VM steps.

checks.workload: 4096 one-KiB records, a rejected conflicting commit and a small commit.
checks.invariant: Zero mid-transaction cache spills; persisted output is complete and every completion restores the ordinary cache size.

checks.workload: Six record families with 2048 existing 41-byte keys and 160-byte values each; 128 FULL commits add six version records apiece.
checks.invariant: The addressed layout writes at most 80% of the predecessor WAL frames through the same provider staging function; both retain every inserted version.

checks.workload: One own data commit followed by a precisely scheduled peer data commit and schema rename, on native SQLite, SQLite Key/Value and redb.
checks.invariant: The own receipt survives adoption, proving no additional read transaction was opened; the adopted sequence excludes the racing peer and the next SQL statement observes its rows and schema.

checks.workload: Native document update followed by a registry metadata write; compare the completed receipt with altered identity.
checks.invariant: Adoption evidence performs zero record reads, matches only the exact receipt, and rejects definition changes.

checks.workload: Eight parameterized INSERT commits on four providers followed by rollback, parameter type mismatch, private DDL and external definition changes.
checks.invariant: One retained analyzed owner across data-only commits, fresh argument results, preserved rollback and PostgreSQL schema diagnostics.

checks.workload: Groups of 2, 64, 65 and 128 pre-evaluated claims, repeated acquisition, competing session and savepoint release.
checks.invariant: Exactly ceil(N/64) table arbitrations for fresh claims, zero extra for unchanged grants; all individual claims and release effects remain present.

checks.workload: 32 inserts, replacement, deletion, search and clear; compare complete graph topology to serial construction.
checks.invariant: Zero whole-graph restorations after own writes; topology and ranked output match the serial owner.

checks.workload: 32 native inserts, replacement, deletion and clear under explicit transactions and autocommit, with a retained reader and rollback.
checks.invariant: Zero whole-graph restorations after own writes, correct ranked results and retained data; explicit rollback performs one validated restore.

checks.workload: 128 rows of one relation, repeated acquisition, savepoint upgrade and final release.
checks.invariant: One registry identity and native relation pin cover all rows; earlier claims survive savepoint undo; final release permits slot reuse with a new generation.

checks.workload: 128 distinct 32-byte keys sharing their leading 24 bytes and the maximum document ID.
checks.invariant: All 128 exact grants coexist with zero per-key registry rows or native relation pins, and final release removes every grant.

checks.workload: One process retains a relation registry while a peer owns temporary dependency admission.
checks.invariant: Unrelated relation lifetime does not block peer admission; cancellation and process-loss release preserve temporary reference ownership.

checks.workload: Plain, encrypted, compressed and combined databases, each initialized as raw, native or Key/Value records.
checks.invariant: A live predecessor prevents all record initialization without writes; release permits initialization and current peers share the same database identity.

checks.workload: A separate process retains the predecessor owner lease layout and zero tag.
checks.invariant: Initialization fails while the predecessor lives and succeeds after process death without deleting coordination files.

checks.workload: Initial native catalog commit and rollback with independent-process nonblocking admission probes.
checks.invariant: Owner admission stays held throughout the physical transaction and is released on either completion path.
